title: Analytica explicatio methodi maximorum et minimorum

deep.reconstruction:
This page solves Problem 2 of E297. The integrand depends on a non-local quantity: Z = Z(x, y, p, q, r, ..., Φ), where Φ(x) = ∫_0^x 𝔷(x, y, p, q, ...) dx is a running integral, p = y', q = y'', and so on. Euler wants the first variation of J = ∫_0^a Z dx.

Step 1. He writes δZ = L δΦ + N δy + P δp + Q δq + ..., with δp = (δy)', δq = (δy)'', etc. (Lagrange-style δ-calculus).

Step 2. Since δΦ(x) = ∫_0^x (𝔑 δy + 𝔓 δp + 𝔔 δq + ...) dx, the non-local term is ∫_0^a L δΦ dx.

Step 3. He integrates this term by parts with V = ∫ L dx. This gives V(a) δΦ(a) − ∫_0^a V (𝔑 δy + 𝔓 δp + ...) dx, using δΦ(0) = 0.

Step 4. He observes that the additive constant in V cancels: C δΦ(a) − C ∫_0^a δ𝔷 = 0. He therefore normalises V(a) = 0, i.e. V(x) = −∫_x^a L dt.

Step 5. The result is δJ = ∫ [(N − V𝔑) δy + (P − V𝔓) δp + (Q − V𝔔) δq + ...] dx. Repeated integration by parts gives the volume term with E = (N − V𝔑) − d(P − V𝔓)/dx + d²(Q − V𝔔)/dx² − ..., plus boundary terms at x = a. These are δy·[(P − V𝔓) − d(Q − V𝔔)/dx + ...], δy'·[(Q − V𝔔) − ...], etc.

Coroll. 1. The answer is Problem 1's answer with N, P, Q, ... replaced by N − V𝔑, P − V𝔓, ....

Coroll. 2. The Euler–Lagrange equation is E = 0. Because V contains the endpoint a, the differential relation between x and y itself depends on the chosen interval: a change of a changes the 'indefinite' relation.

In modern terms, this is the variational problem with an auxiliary state Φ' = 𝔷, Φ(0) = 0. V is (minus) the costate/Lagrange multiplier function, with transversality condition V(a) = 0. The problem serves Euler's programme of recasting the 1744 Methodus inveniendi results (Ch. III, integrands containing indefinite integrals) in Lagrange's δ-algorithm.
errors: No mathematical error. The integration by parts and the normalisation V(a)=0 are correct, given δΦ(0)=0.
Typographically, the last displayed formula on p.120 lacks the closing parenthesis and 'etc.' structure. Its meaning (∫dx[(N−V𝔑)δy+(P−V𝔓)δp+...]) is clear.
Euler silently omits the M dx term in δZ, since x is not varied. This is consistent with his convention.

ideas.what: First variation of a functional whose integrand contains a running integral Φ=∫_0^x 𝔷 dx, handled by integrating by parts with V=∫L dx normalised to vanish at the upper endpoint
ideas.modern_name: Integro-differential (non-local) variational problem; adjoint/costate variable with transversality condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (1744), Ch. III; reformulated here in δ-calculus after Lagrange (1760–62). Costate formalism: Lagrange multipliers / Pontryagin (1950s)
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas (E65, 1744), Ch. III; also E296 'Elementa calculi variationum' context

ideas.what: Observation that the Euler–Lagrange equation for such functionals depends on the endpoint a (non-local character)
ideas.modern_name: Non-locality of extremals for functionals with integral dependence
ideas.where_published: E65 Ch. III, where the value of the integral over the whole interval enters the equation

ideas.what: Substitution rule: replace N,P,Q,... by N−V𝔑, P−V𝔓, ... in the simple case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a δ-calculus restatement of Euler's own 1744 treatment of integrands containing indefinite integrals. The costate interpretation of V is a known retrospective reading in histories of the calculus of variations and optimal control. Nothing new.
